ctor.doc:
A schema as Python. Keyword arguments are the schema's top-level fields (title,
description, author, license, tags, parent, base_compat, task, base, data, purpose,
outputs, targets, footprint, data_policy); `meta` is app/pipeline metadata kept out
of the blackhole/v1 dict (target device, preset quant label, ...).

input.doc:
Declare a knob users set (type text|int|float|bool|enum|model|path, or float/int/str/bool);
spec: default, required, help, min, max, choices, advanced. Returns its reference.

step.doc: Add a stage running op `kind` (ns.op or ns.op@2, or pipeline.<stage>) with its params.

fn.doc:
Call a named function. A job function (forkable pipeline stage) becomes a job.fn
stage; any other becomes a model.edit stage with this one function.

edit.doc: Several named functions in one model.edit stage: [{"fn": "reaq", "avg_bits": 3.5}, ...].

eval.doc: The schema's [eval] table: suites and the final gates the receipt checks.

fields.title: Display name of the recipe.
fields.description: What the recipe does, for people browsing recipes.
fields.author: Who made it (credit BlackHole-Harness for built-ins).
fields.tags: List of short tags: mac, code, moe, ...
fields.parent: id@version of the recipe this one was forked from.
fields.base_compat: Which base models it was tested on.
fields.task: What the result is for (code, chat, ...).
fields.base: The Hugging Face id of the base model, e.g. Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B.
fields.purpose: Free-text purpose that steers calibration data.
fields.footprint: Expected size and memory of the result.
fields.data_policy: Where data may come from and what may leave the machine.
fields.meta: App/pipeline metadata kept out of the schema: {"target": "mac16", "quant": "mlx-3bit"}.

attrs.base: The base model: recipe.base.model (its directory), recipe.base.id

gate.doc: A gate: stop the run (or warn) unless `metric op value` holds.

stepOpts.when: Run only when this holds (a bool or a ${...} reference).
stepOpts.always: Run even after an earlier stage failed a gate.
stepOpts.id: The stage id other steps use to refer to it (default: from the kind or function name).

inputSpec.default: Value used when the user sets nothing.
inputSpec.required: The user must set it (simple mode asks only required, non-advanced inputs).
inputSpec.help: One line shown next to the knob.
inputSpec.choices: Allowed values of an enum input.
inputSpec.advanced: Hide the knob in simple mode.

steps.name: reap
steps.doc: Score experts on calibration text (REAP) and drop the lowest `prune` share.

steps.name: heal
steps.doc: Distil the pruned model back toward the original (shortest verified traces, on-policy rounds).

steps.name: gptq
steps.doc: GPTQ int4 of the routed experts (Hessians from calibration text).

steps.name: reaq
steps.doc: REAQ: per-expert bit widths from REAP rank at a fixed average.

steps.name: mlx
steps.doc: Export to MLX for Apple silicon (HEX experts, attention GPTQ, head/embed bits).

steps.name: qheal
steps.doc: Heal again around the quantized model.

steps.name: bench
steps.doc: LiveCodeBench v6 (and others) on the original and the result.

prune.doc: REAP share of routed experts dropped (best of 2026-10-23: 25%)

gptq_calib.doc: calibration sequences for the GPTQ Hessians (64 was enough on B200)

layer_chunk.doc: MoE layers per sequential GPTQ chunk

reaq_top.doc: share of each layer's experts (by REAP score) on 16-level tables

heal_prompts.doc: fresh calibration-set prompts the teacher answers for distillation

heal_eval_every.doc: optimizer steps between held-out checks (early stopping, best point kept)

heal_calib.doc: prompts for the teacher's answers ("" = the job's calibration set; contest = code_contests)

heal_seq.doc: tokens per training sequence (0 = the job's max_seq); long traces need ~16k

heal_expert_rank.doc: > 0: the routed experts train too, as rank-r updates merged before quantization

heal_layer_weight.doc: > 0: also match every layer's residual stream to the teacher's

heal_router_weight.doc: > 0: routers copy the teacher's preferences among the kept experts

heal_focus.doc: > 0: weight tokens by how much student and teacher disagree (power)

heal_opd_rounds.doc: on-policy distillation rounds after the first pass (student writes, teacher grades)

qheal_minutes.doc: training cap of the heal around the quantized model

heal_samples.doc: > 1 (with heal_calib contest): answers per problem; train on the shortest that passes its tests

mlx_hot.doc: share of each layer's experts (by REAP score) on mlx_hot_bits

mlx_hex.doc: 1: routed experts as HEX per-expert level tables (2**bits levels, block 32, fp8 scales)

mlx_attn_gptq.doc: GPTQ (1) or round-to-nearest (0) for those and the LM head

mlx_qo_bits.doc: q/o projections (the big attention matrices); 0 = mlx_attn_bits

mlx_head_vocab.doc: output-only vocab trim: LM head rows kept (0 = all)

bench.doc: LiveCodeBench release (problems new in it) for original vs int4; "none" skips

bench_models.doc: any of original, int4, reaq, mlx

bench_max_tokens.doc: reasoning models think for tens of thousands of tokens; 4k cut most off

bench_file.doc: a local jsonl in LiveCodeBench's format instead of the download

purpose.doc: Free-text purpose that steers calibration data.

functions.name: add-noise
functions.doc:
Gaussian noise relative to each tensor's std (robustness probes, symmetry breaking for
duplicated experts).

functions.name: bench
functions.doc:
LiveCodeBench pass@1 (Python-only prompt, verbatim) of the models named in `models`: any
of original, pruned, healed, int4, reaq, mlx, or a folder path. One sample per problem, up
to `max_tokens` (reasoning models think for tens of thousands of tokens), the problems new
in `release` (or your own `file` in LiveCodeBench's jsonl format; `limit` > 0 takes the
first n). `budgets` also scores thinking budgets by budget forcing (vLLM only; "" = none).
Each model runs in its own process so the GPU is free between them; a result whose model
folder and settings did not change is reused (the original once per model and settings,
across jobs). Writes work/bench.json; the package step puts it on the model card.

None takes the pipeline's bench knobs (bench "lcb-v6", bench_models, bench_limit,
bench_max_tokens, bench_budgets, bench_file), so this runs exactly what the pipeline's own
bench stage would; bench = "none" there (and no release here) skips it.

functions.name: calibrate
functions.doc:
Get the job ready for the GPU stages: detect the model (config + weight index), plan the
run on this machine, download the weights, and have the teacher (the original model, in
vLLM when it can) write the calibration set: `samples` prompts from `calib` (chat, code,
math, mix, contest, or a file) and their answers, plus the held-out set every KL is measured
on. With `reuse`, an earlier job on the same model and purpose donates its calibration set
and REAP scores, so the teacher is skipped. None leaves a knob as the pipeline has it
(calib "mix", samples 256, REAPer's max_seq).

functions.name: clip-outliers
functions.doc: Clip every weight beyond sigma standard deviations of its tensor.

functions.name: distil
functions.doc:
Distil the REAP-pruned student from the original model (the pipeline's heal stage).
The teacher's answers are the training data unless `data` names a jsonl of rows
{"ids": [...], "start": n} (prompt + answer token ids, answer from `start`), or an earlier
step (traces, your own data function) already wrote work/heal_data.jsonl. Forward KL on the
answer tokens; routed experts, embedding and LM head stay frozen unless expert_rank > 0
(low-rank expert updates); layer_weight / router_weight add layer and router matching;
opd_rounds > 0 adds on-policy rounds (the student writes, the teacher grades every token).
Early stopping on the held-out KL keeps the best point (keep_weights "kl"), or "last"
trains through. Writes <pruned>-healed when it beats the start.

None leaves a knob as the pipeline has it (blackhole_pipeline.DEFAULTS: prompts 1024,
max_tokens 1536, epochs 1.0, accum 8, lr 3e-6, eval_every 8, minutes 45, expert_rank 0,
lora_lr 1e-4, layer_weight 0, router_weight 0, focus 0, opd_rounds 0, opd_prompts 256,
opd_minutes 60, keep_weights "kl"), or as an earlier step set it.

functions.name: drop-experts
functions.doc: Drop the experts a query matches (every MoE layer must end with the same count).

functions.name: drop-layers
functions.doc: Drop whole decoder layers (measured badly on Qwen3-8B: -4 layers cost KL 0.99).

functions.name: duplicate-layers
functions.doc: Depth up-scaling: insert a copy of each listed layer right after it (heal afterwards).

functions.name: fake-quant
functions.doc:
Replace weights with their round-to-nearest value in `format` (to measure a format's
effect end to end on a model that stays 16-bit).

functions.name: fp8-experts
functions.doc:
REAPer's quant stage: the pruned (healed) model with its routed experts in fp8, the
simple vLLM-servable folder REAP classic ships.

functions.name: freeze
functions.doc: Mark the matched parts frozen for training stages (heal, distil).

functions.name: gptq
functions.doc:
GPTQ int4 (group 128) on the routed experts of the pruned (healed, if distil ran) model,
sequentially in chunks of `layer_chunk` MoE layers with Hessians from `calib` calibration
sequences (pipeline defaults 12 and 64: 64 were enough on B200), measured against the
teacher and written as a compressed-tensors W4A16 checkpoint that vLLM serves.

functions.name: hex-pack
functions.doc:
Write the HEX-quantized model in the packed codebook layout (indices, fp8 block scales,
expert scales, tables per tier) that the pipeline's HEX kernels and loaders read. Needs
hex-quantize first. Non-expert tensors are copied as they are.

functions.name: hex-quantize
functions.doc:
HEX: per-expert learned level tables (REAQ marks from `reaq` decide 8 or 16 levels per
expert, else `levels`), fp8 block scales, GPTQ rounding onto the tables when `calib` texts
are given (nearest-level otherwise). Writes the dequantized weights back into the experts
(the saved model loads anywhere) and keeps the headers for hex-pack.

functions.name: merge-similar-experts
functions.doc:
In every MoE layer, merge the `pairs` most similar pairs of experts among the `among`
lowest-scored share (all experts when there are no scores). Similarity is the cosine of the
same `sketch` randomly chosen weights of every expert, so it reads a few KB per expert.
Each merge leaves one expert fewer, so give every layer the same `pairs`.

functions.name: mlx-export
functions.doc:
An MLX folder for Apple silicon from the pruned (healed) model: routed experts GPTQ'd to
`bits` (or, with hex = 1, HEX per-expert learned tables of 2**bits levels, fp8 block scales),
the `hot` share of each layer's experts by REAP score on `hot_bits` (REAQ tiers),
attention / shared experts / dense MLPs at `attn_bits` (q/o at `qo_bits`), embeddings and
LM head at their own bits. head_vocab > 0 trims the output vocab (measured on Qwen3.6: KL
0.070 -> 0.389 for 0.2 GB; leave it 0). think_budget caps thinking at run time (newer
pipelines). None leaves a knob as the pipeline has it (bits 3, group 64, hex 0, hot 0,
hot_bits 4, attn_bits 4, attn_gptq 1, embed_bits 4, head_bits 6).

functions.name: package
functions.doc:
Model cards, receipt.json and RESULTS.md in the job folder, from what every earlier
step measured (KL, top-1, size, bench), and links to the finished models in <job>/out.

functions.name: prune-neurons
functions.doc:
Drop the `ratio` lowest-importance intermediate channels of every dense MLP the query
matches (weight-norm importance; heal afterwards: the dense default prunes 12.5 to 25%).

functions.name: qheal
functions.doc:
Heal AFTER quantization (a BlackHole-Harness original): the student is loaded as exactly
the MLX folder the mlx step wrote (dequantized); routed experts, embedding and LM head stay
frozen at their low-bit values, attention, shared experts and dense MLPs train behind a
straight-through rounding on the folder's own grid, so the gains survive re-quantization.
Trains on the same data as distil (work/heal_data.jsonl) with distil's knobs; `minutes`
caps the training (pipeline default 45). Writes <mlx folder>-healed and points the bench at
it only if it beats the quantized start; otherwise the unhealed folder stands.

functions.name: quant
functions.doc: Give the matched parts a storage format (bf16, fp8, intN, mlxN, nvfp4, hex3, hex4, ...).

functions.name: reap-gpu
functions.doc:
REAP on the GPU (REAPer's pipeline): score every routed expert by router weight x
expert output norm over the calibration set, drop the `ratio` lowest-scored per layer
(pipeline default 0.25; never past 0.5), write the pruned checkpoint, and with `measure`
compare it with the teacher (held-out KL and top-1). Runs calibrate first when it has not
run. The anatomy functions reap-score / reap-prune do the same on the CPU of any machine.

functions.name: reap-prune
functions.doc:
REAP: drop the `ratio` lowest-scored experts of every MoE layer (the same count in
every layer, never below top-k). Needs scores (`scores` on the stage, or load_scores).

functions.name: reap-score
functions.doc:
REAP saliency of every expert over the calibration texts (router weight x expert output
norm, averaged over the tokens routed to it), written onto the experts as score / freq /
rank. `calib` is a list of texts or token-id lists, or a path to a .jsonl / .txt file.

functions.name: reaq
functions.doc: REAQ: REAP scores pick each expert's format so the average lands at avg_bits.

functions.name: reaq-codebook
functions.doc:
REAQ per-expert codebooks on the GPU (a BlackHole-Harness original): the `top` share of
each layer's experts by REAP score get 16-level learned tables, the rest 8-level, blocks of
`block` weights with fp8 scales, GPTQ rounding onto the tables (pipeline defaults 0.5 and
32). Measured against the teacher and int4; the packed indices, tables and scales are
saved. The anatomy functions reaq + hex-quantize do the same on the CPU.

functions.name: reorder-by-score
functions.doc:
Sort every MoE layer's experts by REAP score, highest first: hot experts get the low
ids, one contiguous range per tier for tiered kernels and hot/cold placement.

functions.name: router-temperature
functions.doc: Divide router logits by t (t > 1 spreads the load, t < 1 sharpens the routing).

functions.name: scale
functions.doc: Multiply the matched weights by `factor`.

functions.name: traces
functions.doc:
Verified shortest-trace distillation data (a BlackHole-Harness original). The teacher
solves `problems` competitive-programming problems (deepmind/code_contests, pre-2022, so
not in LiveCodeBench's newer releases, or your own `file` in LiveCodeBench's jsonl format)
`samples` times each; every answer's code runs against the problem's tests on the CPU, and
`keep` = "shortest" trains the student on the shortest answer that passed ("all": every
passing answer). Only answers that ended on their own count. `think_budget` > 0 cuts
thinking still open at that many tokens and tells the teacher to answer now (budget forcing).
Writes work/heal_data.jsonl (rows {ids, start}) for distil, and work/heal_traces.json.

functions.name: train
functions.doc: Mark the matched parts trainable for training stages (heal, distil).

functions.name: trim-head
functions.doc: Output-only vocab trim: keep these token ids (or the JSON list in `file`) in the LM head.

functions.name: zero-small
functions.doc:
Unstructured magnitude pruning: zero the smallest `fraction` of every matrix (the file
does not shrink; it measures what a sparse kernel could skip).

ops.name: convert.moefy
ops.doc:
LAB ONLY: measured negative. On Qwen3-8B (B200, 2026-10-23) 64 experts at top-32 cost
KL 0.53 (0.39 with an oracle router): SiLU FFNs are not sparse enough to split cleanly,
and REAP on the new routers pruned about as badly as random (KL 0.67 vs 0.71). Dense
models use score.neurons + prune.neurons; REAP stays for real MoEs.

MoEfication: split every FFN's intermediate neurons into `experts` groups and train a
small router per layer to pick `top_k` of them per token, so the dense model becomes a
MoE with the same weights. Then REAP can score and drop whole experts, and inference
only computes the chosen ones.

  split   cluster   k-means on each neuron's up/gate weight vectors (parameter clustering)
          coact     balanced graph partition of neuron co-activation on the data (the
                    MoEfication paper's best split; needs activations, so slower)
          random    equal random groups (a baseline)
  router  mlp       a linear (or 2-layer) router trained to predict which groups hold the
                    largest activations, on `router_tokens` tokens of the data so far
          centroid  no training: score each expert by the token's similarity to its
                    neurons' mean weight vector
  shared  fraction of neurons kept always on as a shared expert (the ones active on most
          tokens), which the LLaMA-MoE line of work found steadies quality

Output is a standard MoE checkpoint so every later op and runtime loads it:
Mixtral layout for Llama-style attention, Qwen3-MoE layout for Qwen3 (qk-norm),
Qwen2-MoE layout when attention has biases or a shared expert is kept. Metrics:
recon_kl (dense vs moefied on held-out text before any pruning), router_recall (share
of the true top activation mass the router picks), active_b.

data.help: text for co-activation statistics and router training (the data so far)

top_k.help: experts per token; active FFN share = top_k / experts

router_tokens.help: tokens of activations the routers train on

router_hidden.help: 0 = linear router; >0 = 2-layer MLP of this width

shared.help: share of neurons kept always on as a shared expert, e.g. 0.125

ops.name: data.dataset
ops.doc: A public or local dataset, filtered to the licence allow-list in data_policy.

source.help: hf:<repo>[:split] | path to .jsonl | bhdata kits dir

ops.name: data.decontam
ops.doc: Drop rows that share n-grams with eval suites or carry their canaries.

ops.name: data.mix
ops.doc: Weighted mix of datasets, deduplicated and shuffled.

ops.name: data.own_rollouts
ops.doc:
The current model answers prompts; answers that pass a checker (tests, a judge, an
exact match) become training rows. llmap exp02's 12% -> 80% came from this.

ops.name: data.teacher_gen
ops.doc:
The teacher writes prompts for a purpose and answers them. With a purpose it lists
sub-tasks, writes varied self-contained requests for each, mixes in the closest public
preset, and answers every prompt; held-out answers are kept back for eval.

On a B200 the stage's time goes to vLLM startup and the prompt-writer rounds, not the
answers, so the port keeps the written topics and prompts as their own cached files
(keyed by teacher + purpose + writer settings, reused when only samples or answer
settings change) and keeps one vLLM server up across the writer and answer rounds.

model.help: teacher; defaults to the base model

purpose.help: free text; empty uses the preset in `preset`

topics.help: sub-skills of the purpose (e.g. from the schema builder); empty = the teacher lists its own

samples.help: prompts to generate and answer; 64 calibration sequences scored as well as 256 on Qwen3-30B-A3B (B200, 2026-10-23)

purpose_mix.help: share taken from the closest public preset

teacher.help: local (vLLM, else transformers) | frontier:<model> (Claude/GPT, needs a key and spend cap)

ops.name: distil.kd
ops.doc: Distil a teacher into a different (usually smaller, dense) student.

model.help: student; defaults to the last model in the chain

max_minutes.help: wall-clock cap; training stops, merges and saves

student.help: HF id of the student when it is not the chain's model

ops.name: eval.agreement
ops.doc:
Model vs teacher on held-out teacher answers. Metrics: top1_agreement, kl,
ppl_teacher, ppl_model.

ops.name: eval.bench
ops.doc:
Public suites run on the model (vLLM for safetensors, llama-server for GGUF), with
a paired bootstrap interval against the base model's reading. Metrics per suite:
<suite>, <suite>_lo, <suite>_hi, <suite>_kept (share of the base score).

ops.name: eval.footprint
ops.doc:
Measured memory of the model served the way the target will run it: GGUF bytes
(counted once) plus all buffers of a one-slot llama-server at the schema's context
and KV type, after a prompt of 3/4 of the context. Metrics: file_gb, footprint_gb,
tok_s (when the target device class is known), fits.

device.help: device class for the tok/s estimate, e.g. 8GB-VRAM, M-series-16GB

ops.name: heal.kd
ops.doc:
Heal a pruned or quantised model toward its unpruned teacher: SFT on the teacher's
answers, plus logit KL when kd_weight > 0. NaN/inf steps are skipped.

Always a trained distillation. A closed-form, no-training heal (refitting the next
layer by least squares) made Qwen3-8B worse in every B200 test (2026-10-23), so there
is no such mode: heal with training, or leave the stage out.

model.help: student; defaults to the last model in the chain

max_minutes.help: wall-clock cap; training stops, merges and saves

kd_weight.help: weight of logit KL to the teacher; 0 = plain SFT

fake_quant.help: heal against fake-quantised weights of this GGUF type map (final heal)

ops.name: heal.route_anneal
ops.doc:
Post-train a MoEfied model to route: start with every expert on (exactly the dense
model), then step the active experts down along `schedule`, distilling from the dense
teacher at each step (router straight-through gate + load-balance aux loss). LAB.

model.help: MoEfied student; defaults to the last model in the chain

schedule.help: experts on per token, one distillation step each

max_minutes.help: wall-clock budget, split equally over the schedule

ops.name: lab.script
ops.doc:
Run a Python file's run(ctx). Inputs are any artifacts passed in `inputs`; the
script writes to ctx.out(name) for each name in `outputs` and may report metrics.

file.help: path to the .py file, relative to the schema

code_sha256.help: pinned hash of the file; the cache key includes it

ops.name: merge.lora
ops.doc: Merge a LoRA adapter directory into a model.

ops.name: model.detect
ops.doc:
Read config.json, the safetensors index and tokenizer_config.json (a few KB, never
the weights) and record what the model is: kinds (moe, dense, hybrid, vision), experts,
top-k, shared experts, layer split, sizes, dtype, quantisation, KV bytes per token,
chat template, remote code. The runner adds it as the first stage of every run, puts
the result in ${base.*}, and refuses the run if the schema's targets or any stage's
needs do not match, before anything is downloaded.

model.help: Hugging Face id or local directory; defaults to the job's base

ops.name: model.edit
ops.doc:
Run named functions from blackhole_dev on the model so far and write the result
as a new checkpoint with a receipt (blackhole-anatomy.json). One stage = one function
(`fn` with its params flat on the stage) or several (`steps`, a list of {fn, ...} tables).
Structural edits (REAP pruning, merges, layer splices) are byte copies; weight edits and
HEX quantization compute on CPU unless the function loads the model (`device`). `scores`
attaches REAP scores (a saliency artifact) before the functions run; `functions` names
.py files or modules whose @function definitions the schema uses, pinned by sha256 in
the receipt. Every function's returned metrics land in metrics.json (gates read them).

fn.help: a named function, e.g. reap-prune, reaq, hex-quantize, or your own

select.help: which parts the function works on (a query), when it takes one

scores.help: REAP scores to attach first, e.g. ${score.saliency}

functions.help: modules or .py files (relative to the schema) defining extra functions

pack.help: "hex" writes the packed HEX layout instead of a plain checkpoint

force.help: save even if the result would not load with stock loaders

ops.name: model.fetch
ops.doc:
Download the base model to $BLACKHOLE_HOME/models/<org>--<name>. The runner adds
this as the second stage (`weights`) unless the base model is a local directory.

ops.name: package.gguf
ops.doc:
The GGUF plus an Ollama Modelfile with the right chat and tool-call template, and
a LM Studio / llama.cpp run line.

ops.name: package.hf
ops.doc: Model card, schema, receipt and eval next to the safetensors; manifest.sha256.

ops.name: plan.fit
ops.doc:
Pick the gentlest recipe that meets a file-size target by walking a ladder, gentlest
first: quantise harder before pruning. The default ladder is the dense frontier on
Qwen3-8B (B200, 2026-10-23, GPTQ):
    Q4_K_M            ~6.1 GB  KL 0.028
    Q3_K_M            ~5.3 GB  KL 0.15   (beats every pruned recipe of similar size)
    Q3_K_M + 12.5%    ~5.0 GB  KL 0.25
    Q3_K_M + 25%
Reports metrics later stages read: bits, prune (0 when none), need_prune, predicted_gb,
fits. If the last rung misses the target, fits is false and the schema's gate stops the
run with the reason; layer dropping is never on the ladder (KL 0.99 for 4 layers).

MoE models use the same shape with experts as the prunable part (moe-prune-int4):
    REAP 25% + Q4_K_M  ~10.4 GB experts  KL 0.034   (Qwen3-30B-A3B, GPTQ)
    REAP 25% + Q3_K_M
    REAP 37.5% + Q3_K_M  6.9 GB          KL 0.121   (50% + int4 at the same size: 0.171)
Pruning never goes past 50%: past that every MoE and dense run fell apart.

Planned (not on the ladder yet): once quant.expert_codebook has a real kernel and a
packed format, "REAP 25% + REAQ codebooks" replaces the Q3_K_M tiers for MoE. Lab
numbers (Qwen3-30B-A3B, B200, 2026-10-23, simulated quant): 16/8-level REAQ tables with
GPTQ rounding KL 0.033 at 9.5 GB vs Q4_K_M rung 0.034 at 10.4 GB; near 9 GB the best goes
from 0.074 (REAP 37.5% + GPTQ int4) to 0.041. Not added now because nothing can serve it.

It estimates the GGUF file from ${base.params_b} and the prunable share of the weights, so
it runs on the CPU in a second. The frontier's sizes were safetensors with 16-bit
embeddings, so GGUF files are smaller (Qwen3-8B Q4_K_M ~5.0 GB); eval.footprint
measures the real file at the end.

ffn_share.help: share of weights pruning can remove: FFNs in dense LLMs (~0.6-0.7)

prunable_b.help: billions of prunable weights instead of ffn_share, e.g. ${base.expert_params_b} for MoE

ladder.help: rungs tried in order, gentlest first

ops.name: prune.neurons
ops.doc:
Remove the lowest-scored FFN neurons and rewrite the checkpoint with a smaller
intermediate size per layer (still a standard dense checkpoint every runtime loads).
Protect rules: the critical set from score.neurons is never removed, the top
`protect_top` share of each layer is kept, the first and last `skip_edge` layers are
untouched, and no layer drops more than `max_layer` of its neurons.

ratio.help: share of FFN neurons removed overall; the dense frontier is still being measured

allocation.help: global (rank all layers together, capped by max_layer) | uniform

protect_critical.help: never remove neurons score.neurons marked critical

protect_top.help: share of each layer's best neurons always kept

skip_edge.help: first and last layers left whole

max_layer.help: most any one layer may lose

multiple_of.help: round each layer's new size for fast kernels

ops.name: prune.reap
ops.doc:
Keep the top experts per layer by saliency and rewrite the checkpoint shard by
shard in its own format (fp8 blocks and MXFP4 survive). CPU only.

ratio.help: share of routed experts dropped in every MoE layer

keep_groups_even.help: DeepSeek-style groups keep the same count per group

ops.name: prune.structured
ops.doc:
Dense models: keep a fraction of each FFN's channels and of the KV groups, and drop
whole layers, chosen on the data so far. Heal afterwards.

drop_layers.help: banned in defaults: dropping 4 layers of Qwen3-8B cost KL 0.99

ops.name: qat.block_ap
ops.doc:
Quantisation-aware training block by block: each quantised block is trained to
reproduce the full-precision block's outputs, then the scales are frozen.

ops.name: qat.ste
ops.doc:
QAT to one GGUF type with straight-through rounding: every weight trains computing
as llama.cpp will store it. The following quant.gguf must use that type, no imatrix.

model.help: student; defaults to the last model in the chain

max_minutes.help: wall-clock cap; training stops, merges and saves

ops.name: quant.expert_codebook
ops.doc:
Per-expert codebook quantisation (HEX, Header-Encoded eXperts; op name kept for now). EXPERIMENTAL,
a BlackHole-Harness original.

NVFP4-style layout: weights in 16-weight blocks with an FP8 scale per block, and on top
each expert carries a header (an FP32 scale plus a learned value table of 8 or 16 levels)
that the low-bit indices point into. The table is fitted per expert (k-means on the
block-normalised weights, weighted by the imatrix when data is given). With a type map
from quant.reaq (target="codebook") each expert gets its own table size.

Rounding is GPTQ onto the codebook by default: columns are quantised to the nearest table
level in order, and each column's error is pushed onto the not-yet-quantised columns
through the calibration Hessian, exactly as quant.gptq does onto llama.cpp grids.

Measured (B200, 2026-10-23, Qwen3-30B-A3B at REAP 25%, simulated quant, 32 held-out
answers). The pieces stack:
    GPTQ int3, uniform                        3.25 bpw           KL 0.083
    8-level tables, nearest rounding          3.25 bpw (8.23 GB) KL 0.066
    8-level tables, GPTQ rounding             3.25 bpw           KL 0.054
    uniform 8-level / random split / REAQ     3.5 bpw            KL 0.049 / 0.047 / 0.041
    REAQ 16/8 levels, GPTQ rounding           9.5 GB             KL 0.033 (GPTQ int4 0.034 at 10.4 GB)
A per-expert scale alone does nothing; at 4 bits a per-expert 16-level table with nearest
rounding only ties NVFP4. Lab until it generalises (next: gpt-oss-20b) and a real kernel
exists; then "REAP 25% + REAQ codebooks" replaces plan.fit's MoE int3 tiers.

Serving: no packed format yet. It needs a custom kernel, or a llama.cpp/vLLM patch that
reads the per-expert header and does the table lookup in the expert matmul. Until then the
output is fake-quantised bf16 safetensors plus the headers and indices for measuring.

data.help: calibration text for the GPTQ Hessians and imatrix weighting; the data so far by default

type_map.help: per-expert table sizes from quant.reaq (target=codebook), e.g. ${reaq.type_map}; empty uses `levels` for all

levels.help: table size when there is no type map: 8 (3-bit indices) | 16 (4-bit)

block.help: weights per block, each with its own scale

header.help: per-expert header precision: scale and table

fit.help: kmeans | lloyd_max | nf (fixed NormalFloat table, the ablation)

rounding.help: gptq: error-compensated onto the table, needs data | nearest (the ablation)

experts_only.help: attention, routers, shared experts and the head keep their types

export.help: fake_quant (bf16 safetensors + headers) | packed (needs the kernel; not implemented)

ops.name: quant.fp8_experts
ops.doc:
Routed experts to fp8 with 128x128 block scales; attention, routers, shared experts
and the head stay bf16. For vLLM serving on a GPU box.

ops.name: quant.gguf
ops.doc:
Write the GGUF with llama-quantize from a type map (or a single type), then the
parity checks: every tensor as mapped, size within 0.5% of plan, KLD and top-1 vs
a bf16 GGUF of the same weights, llama-tokenize == HF.

Never plain round-to-nearest: either the weights come from quant.gptq already snapped
to this GGUF grid (packed exactly, no imatrix), or llama-quantize gets an imatrix.
On Qwen3-8B (B200, 2026-10-23) GPTQ int4 had 2.5x less KL than round-to-nearest.

imatrix.help: required unless the model came from quant.gptq on this type's grid

pre_snapped.help: the weights are already on the grid (after quant.gptq): pack them exactly

ops.name: quant.gguf_map
ops.doc:
Plan a per-tensor GGUF type map under a size budget: expert bit widths from REAP
layer importance x imatrix output energy, fixed types for attention, embeddings, head.
Writes the map and its predicted file size; does not quantise.

max_gb.help: file budget; 0 = footprint.max_gb minus KV and buffers

head.help: output layer type (BH keeps an 8-bit head)

ops.name: quant.gptq
ops.doc:
GPTQ: quantise each layer's weights column by column, pushing every rounding error
onto the columns not yet quantised using the layer's input Hessian from calibration
text, so the layer's output changes as little as possible. Writes a model whose weights
already sit on the target grid:
  gguf:<type>   llama.cpp's block grids (Q4_K, Q3_K, Q5_K, Q6_K; scales per super-block),
                so quant.gguf with pre_snapped packs them bit-exactly (llmap kquant.py
                has the grid code)
  int<b>-g<n>   plain group-wise integers for vLLM (GPTQ/Marlin kernels, compressed-tensors)

Qwen3-8B, B200, 2026-10-23: int4 6.1 GB KL 0.028 (round-to-nearest 0.070), int3 5.3 GB
KL 0.15, better than any pruned recipe of similar size.

data.help: calibration text; the data so far

grid.help: gguf:<type> | int4-g128 | int3-g128 | typemap:<path> (per-tensor grids, e.g. from quant.reaq)

damp.help: Hessian dampening, as a share of its mean diagonal

act_order.help: quantise columns in order of decreasing Hessian diagonal

ops.name: quant.mlx
ops.doc:
MLX folders for Apple silicon: Q<bits> group quantisation, or DWQ<bits> that trains
the scales so next-token distributions match the full model on the data so far.

ops.name: quant.reaq
ops.doc:
REAQ, Router-weighted Expert Activation Quantization: a BlackHole-Harness original
(2026-10-23). EXPERIMENTAL until the GPU thread's interval test reports.

REAP's router-weighted activation score (saliency x routing frequency per expert) sets
each expert's bit width inside an interval [min_bits, max_bits]: experts the purpose
leans on get more bits, rarely used ones fewer, under a byte budget (a knapsack over
expert x type, cost = bytes, value = score-weighted error of the type). No expert is
removed. Attention, router, shared experts and the head keep fixed types.

Earlier history: a first version (2026-10-23, then called expert_bits, allowing 2-bit and
pruning the coldest experts) lost to uniform int4/int3 at equal size by 0.01-0.04 KL,
most likely because rare experts went to 2 bits; hence the interval, which keeps every
expert at min_bits or above. Uniform GPTQ per-layer quant is the baseline to beat.

MoE only, floor 3 bits (B200, 2026-10-23): on a dense model MoEfied to experts, REAQ
lost to uniform GPTQ at both budgets (int4 0.028 vs best mix 0.031; int3 0.108 vs 0.24),
and every interval reaching down to 2-bit was bad. Params reject a Q2 floor.

Runtimes store a layer's experts as one fused tensor of one type, so the plan is
realised by `layout`:
  safetensors  per-expert quantisation configs for a custom torch/vLLM loader
               (what the GPU thread's interval test measures)
  bands        sort experts by score and split each layer's fused tensors into 2-4
               bands (hot/warm/cold), one type per band; needs the harness's
               llama.cpp patch that loads banded expert tensors
  layer        one type per layer (stock llama.cpp and Ollama); this averages REAQ's
               per-expert choice away, so it is only a fallback
Writes the type map quant.gptq / quant.gguf consume, the expert permutation, and the
predicted size and error.

target="codebook" picks a value-table size per expert for quant.expert_codebook instead
of a GGUF type (B200, 2026-10-23, Qwen3-30B-A3B at REAP 25%: top 50% experts by REAP
score on 16-level tables, the rest on 8-level, KL 0.036 at 4.0 bpw vs 0.043 for a random
split: the first per-expert allocation that beat uniform).

data.help: text for measuring each type's error per expert (imatrix); empty uses the score only

max_gb.help: expert byte budget; 0 = footprint.max_gb minus the fixed parts and KV

min_bits.help: the interval's floor: no expert goes below it

score.help: value per expert: saliency | freq | saliency*freq | a lab op's column

layout.help: safetensors | bands (needs the llama.cpp patch) | layer (fallback)

target.help: bits: a GGUF type per expert in [min_bits, max_bits] | codebook: a table size per expert for quant.expert_codebook

levels.help: codebook target: the table sizes to choose between, smallest first

hot_share.help: codebook target: share of experts (by score) that get the largest table; 0 = solve under max_gb

ops.name: quant.w4a16
ops.doc:
4-bit weights, 16-bit activations for vLLM on Ada/Hopper: quant.gptq with an int4
grid, written as compressed-tensors with an fp8 head.

ops.name: rft.self
ops.doc:
Rejection-sampling fine-tune on the model's own passing answers, in rounds. A round
is kept only if held-out KL drops and paired pass@1 does not fall (BH round rule).

model.help: student; defaults to the last model in the chain

max_minutes.help: wall-clock cap; training stops, merges and saves

ops.name: score.neurons
ops.doc:
Activation-scored importance of every FFN neuron (intermediate channel) of a dense
model on the calibration text: mean |activation| x norm of its down-projection column
(Wanda-style), plus the critical set: neurons whose activations are massive outliers
(> `massive` x the layer median) and those carrying super weights. Same JSON layout as
REAP's table, per layer and per neuron, so prune and quant ops read either.

B200 on Qwen3-8B (2026-10-23): 25% pruned by this score gave KL 0.24 (expert-norm 0.26,
MoEfy+REAP 0.67); random 50% destroyed the model, so the critical set matters.

massive.help: activation outlier factor that marks a neuron critical

ops.name: score.reap
ops.doc:
REAP saliency per expert: router-weighted expert activation norms over the
calibration tokens, with hooks on every router of any HF MoE (moe.py).

The saliency artifact is a shared score table other ops read (prune.reap,
quant.reaq, quant.gguf_map, lab ops): JSON
{"layers": [{"layer": 3, "experts": [{"id": 0, "saliency": S_j, "freq": share of tokens
routed to j, "gate_mean": mean g_j(x) when routed, "out_norm": mean ||f_j(x)||}, ...]}],
"tokens": n, "model": id}. S_j = mean over tokens routed to j of g_j(x)*||f_j(x)||.

answers.help: score on prompt + answer, not prompts only

ops.name: sft.lora
ops.doc: Plain supervised fine-tune with a merged LoRA.

model.help: student; defaults to the last model in the chain

max_minutes.help: wall-clock cap; training stops, merges and saves

ops.name: sync.bucket
ops.doc:
Upload the job's outputs, receipt and logs to an S3-compatible bucket (or `hf
upload`), each artifact under its cache key, so a fresh VM restores whatever matches
instead of recomputing it. Use with `always: true`; `shutdown` powers the VM off after.

ops.name: vocab.trim
ops.doc:
Keep the tokens seen in the data (plus specials and byte fallbacks), remap the
tokenizer, slice embedding and head. Checks llama-tokenize == HF after.

examples.layers[0:4].attn: attention of the first four layers
examples.layers[*].moe.experts[rank<0.25]: the bottom quarter of every layer's experts by REAP score
